chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Rib'i from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Then let them end their untidiness' [and] 'the combing of the man with perfume.'

key_terms.تَفَثَهُمْ: Their untidiness or grooming (referring to removing hair/nails and applying perfume)
key_terms.حُفُوفُ: Combing or brushing (specifically of the hair)
key_terms.عَزَّ وَ جَلَّ: The Mighty and Majestic (honorific for Allah)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'end their untidiness' (tafath) specifically refer to in the context of Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the meaning of 'tafath' (removal of impurities or unkemptness) in the context of Hajj rites, linking it to personal grooming such as combing hair and applying perfume. It reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of interpreting Quranic commands through the lens of Imami jurisprudence, emphasizing that the prohibition of certain grooming acts during Ihram is lifted or redefined for specific rituals. The hadith underscores the balance between ritual purity and physical cleanliness in Islamic worship.
